key_insight: PerovAgent autonomously improves ligand binding on halide perovskite surfaces while turning search observations into testable chemical design principles.
engineering_relevance: The framework could guide surface-capping ligand selection for perovskite nanocrystals by coupling molecular optimization with statistically evaluated design rules.
method: Use LLM-driven multi-agent reasoning to propose and refine ligand chemistries.
Construct atomistic models and evaluate binding energies with machine-learned interatomic potentials.
Prospectively test proposed design principles, audit confounders, and examine a recurring principle with DFT.
evidence_signal: Across 10 independent CsPbBr3 campaigns, binding-energy objectives improved; 19 of 35 principles gained prospective support, seven also passed the confound audit, and DFT reproduced the predicted alkynyl-phosphonate energetic preference.
watch_item: Improved computed binding energies do not establish experimental nanocrystal performance, and most proposed principles did not pass both prospective testing and confound auditing.
paper_title: PerovAgent: Autonomous Ligand Design for Halide Perovskite Nanocrystals
